title: [A] Trace and troubleshoot a request from browser to backend
brief: A customer reports that the new version of a notes website works on one laptop but fails on another. Both can browse other websites. Trace the request from name resolution to backend processing and ask for the observations needed to locate the fault. Defend one safe corrective action.

clarifications.question: What exact failure is reported?
clarifications.answer: The failing laptop reports a certificate-name mismatch, before any HTTP status is received.

clarifications.question: What changed?
clarifications.answer: The public address changed this morning. The new edge serves notes.example.test; the old edge now serves a different hostname.

clarifications.question: What do DNS and connections show?
clarifications.answer: The failing laptop resolved the old address before cutover. A fresh connection still reaches that old address using its cached answer.

clarifications.question: Are application data and credentials affected?
clarifications.answer: No data corruption is observed. Do not bypass certificate verification.

hints: Separate DNS, connection, TLS, and HTTP observations.
Ask which identity the certificate authenticates.
A TTL change cannot retroactively replace earlier cached answers.
changes: The API handler logs contain no request from the failing client. Explain whether adding backend replicas helps.
The old edge can be restored temporarily. Describe the safe migration overlap.
referenceSolution: Start by asking for the exact symptom and boundary. A certificate-name mismatch establishes that some endpoint was reached but did not authenticate for the intended name. Obtain the DNS answer and actual connection destination, compare cached versus fresh resolution, and verify which certificate the reached edge presents. The backend handler has not received the HTTP request, so adding replicas does not address the immediate cause. Restore valid service and certificate coverage on the old edge while cached answers and connections drain, validate the new edge, and monitor fresh verified handshakes. Do not disable verification, use a raw IP as an equivalent identity test, or assert that a newly lowered TTL immediately reaches all caches. Explain the distinction between a diagnostic cache refresh on one laptop and the fleet-safe migration fix.
debrief: Review whether you localized the failure before proposing changes. Strong reasoning uses the observed certificate error to narrow the boundary while retaining alternatives until destination evidence arrives. An initial wrong hypothesis is acceptable if you revise it using evidence. Retry with a connection-refused symptom and describe how the first investigation changes.
